reviews.text:
Avoid LAASER Animal Hospital — they have great doctors and staff, but their billing practices prey on desperate pet owners.

When your pet is sick, you'll pay whatever it takes. LAASER knows that, and its billing practices are built around it.

Before my dog was even examined, I was required to pay $1,200 for an "evaluation." Staff openly admitted this was more than the evaluation would cost. They said they needed "wiggle room" and that I'd be refunded the difference later. Then I was told he might need to be hospitalized for 48 hours, and I was required to pay another $6,000 upfront. That estimate included services that were never provided. Again, I was told it was more than the actual cost and that I'd get a refund.

He was hospitalized for less than 24 hours.

It has now been more than three weeks. I have not received an itemized invoice showing what services were actually performed or what they actually cost. I have not received a single dollar back. I've called numerous times, and each time I've been brushed off with no answers and no timeline.

Requiring thousands of dollars in deliberate overpayment, then sitting on that money with no accounting, is unacceptable. It's even worse when it's done to people who are scared and just trying to do right by their pets. All of the doctors and staff were very nice, but these billing practices are unethical and unacceptable.

LAASER was able to care for my dog during an emergency. They were able to take him in a reasonable time and administered the care he needed. The  previous hospital we tried said we had a 4 hr then a 12 hour wait before he could be seen by a veterinarian. LAASER provided care 10 minutes after we arrived. They were pleasant and whisked us through their check-in process. Thanks to them, Our dog was fine and we were able to pick him up next day.

Absolutely the worst possible ER you can bring your pet to. They take FOREVER, the staff is rude, they leave your pet unattended for 8+ hours with no updates for the pet parents and their pricing is ridiculous i was quoted $9,000 for a ONE day hospitalization. That is unheard of!!! Do NOT go here if you care about your pet please i beg of you. This is coming from someone that has 11+ years of vet tech, dog training and grooming experience 🙏🏼

I never leave reviews but I have never heard of such bad service.

I DO NOT recommend coming here.

I’ve been in the veterinary field for years and I cannot believe the service my brother and his suffering dog got tonight. Previously his Frenchie was here for spinal issues and they suggested she had IVDD and gave my brother a poor prognosis. Her symptoms haven’t worsened, up until the past few days. She has very clear spinal deformities, limping, panting like crazy, hadn’t eaten anything in the last 2 days and despite being on 5 different pain medications, she is still SCREAMING in pain.

My brother made the very painful decision to euthanize his dear baby and the doctors/ techs on staff gaslit my brother and told him she is in “too good of a state to ethically euthanize her tonight” and at this hour it is too late to find another clinic. I’m disgusted at the horrible bed side manners of this place. Now she will have to suffer even longer and we hope she can make it through the night or until we can find another vet that can help. To make matters worse, the techs/ veterinarians were rude and even rolled their eyes during the visit. This is not how potential euthanasia appointments should go and this has been the whole situation even more stressful than it has to be.

Side note: the receptionist I spoke to seemed very sweet and understanding.

I don't normally leave reviews, but wanted to share about my great experience with this vet.

My dog was having a medical emergency and our regular vet could not fit her in, but recommended that I take her to LAASER. I was very nervous to bring her in because of the relatively low reviews, but ultimately had a very positive experience. Every staff member I interacted with from the front desk to the techs to the vet, were very attentive and kind. They were very transparent about pricing and helped me figured out what my dog needed / didn't need that day. They also sent me home with antibiotics for my dog at no cost, which was very thoughtful and appreciated.

Thank you, LAASER!

I’m extremely disappointed with our experience here. I brought my dog to the ER twice in the same day. The first time, we were there from approximately 10 AM–3 PM, and then we had to return that same night and were there from approximately 10 PM–6:30 AM. I then left her there until around 3 PM so she could have an ultrasound. Between the visits, imaging, ultrasound, and treatment, I spent approximately $4,000.

During the first visit, only her abdomen was X-rayed. When we returned that night, her esophagus was only X-rayed because I specifically requested it. She ultimately left on additional medications and increased doses of medications she was already taking, bringing her to around 10 medications total.

Two days after leaving the ER, Millie pooped out a hard, sharp piece of plastic.

I immediately contacted the hospital because I was concerned that there could be additional foreign material or an obstruction and asked for a comped repeat X-ray. After spending nearly $4,000 and all the hours Millie had already spent being evaluated, their response was essentially, “If you feel the need for an X-ray, you can come in, but you have to pay.”

I understand that foreign objects aren’t always visible on imaging and that no diagnostic test is perfect. What I find unacceptable is the lack of concern or willingness to follow up after learning that she had actually passed a sharp foreign object only two days after being discharged.

I wasn’t asking for anything unreasonable. I wanted to make sure my dog was safe and that nothing else had been missed. After spending nearly $4,000 and putting Millie through hours and hours of testing, I expected much more concern and accountability.

Unfortunately, this experience has left me with very little confidence in returning here for emergency care. Do yourself a favor and find a different hospital where they actually care about the well being of your animal and not how much money they can make.

LAASER is really a top notch place. You’d hope you don’t end up here but if you do you’ll be well taken care of. They are very attentive and have a triage process to make sure they get to every animal in need, so in my case I ended up waiting awhile but my dog wasn’t in bad shape compared to those coming in. The doctors, nurses and all the staff is really considerate and Hudson my dog has always received the best care while there the few times I’ve had to come. I can’t say enough good things!

Great care, efficient, but most of all- compassionate. I love so many of the techs who work here. It’s one of the most difficult jobs to work a 24/7 animal ER- you see so much pain and grief. Somehow, quite a lot of the staff here still retain that empathy and softness in spite of everything. Rena for me is a stand out- she went above and beyond for me and my girls, more than most vets would ever do. Yes, prices are higher here than a lot of primary vets, but very standard for animal emergency rooms, and they have consistently refunded me a percentage of my deposits after treatment without prompting. Thank you for taking such good care of my girls, LAASER.
Expensive but good doctors and friendly staff; clean.
They saved my dog’s life. Thank you ED vet Dr. Jasper & Dr. Vitt and everyone at LAASER.

Scam place , wanted to charge me 1500$ for treatment although they were not sure what’s wrong with the cat , I said no thanks still had to pay 200 for consultation fee! Waiting in the lobby we find out they haven’t been giving the cat water in the back and felt like they kidnapped the cat, the cat had blisters from not drinking water in the mouth as it was hot, anyway I am glad I got not treatment as the cat was perfectly fine when we got home

I have brought my cats here before for after-hours emergencies, but I am extremely disappointed with how they handled my third kitten, Lucy.I found Lucy very sick on the street, and she looked like she had little hope of surviving. When you bring a seriously ill animal to an emergency facility, you expect compassion, urgency, and professional care. Instead, I was told that the doctor would see other emergencies first and I was left waiting while my kitten was very sick.I explained that I was financially responsible for Lucy and was willing to take responsibility for her care. I was ultimately told to clean her eyes and give her regular milk with wet food. While I appreciate that I was not charged for the visit, that does not change how disappointed I was with the lack of compassion and urgency shown toward a vulnerable stray kitten.
I understand that emergency hospitals have to prioritize cases, but I believe every animal deserves to be treated with compassion and respect, especially when they are seriously ill and have been brought in by someone trying to save their life.
After this experience, I no longer feel comfortable bringing my pets here. Unfortunately, the way Lucy was handled left me feeling that this is not a place where I can trust my animals to receive the compassion and professional care they deserve.

If you have an emergency with your pet I advise to go to any other emergency vet. The only reason I went here was because the ER vet that is in my area was closed that night. This place was my next option but they are so disorganized and lack communication. When I got there no one was at the front desk. They lacked communicating how serious my baby's situation was. Maybe they do but they don't seem to do triage to determine which animal needs to be seen first based on their condition and instead are vague and try to make you pay thousands to get your pet seen first. Not only that but  both the vet and vet techs were so cold and almost robotic. They also told me if I took her home she may not live when I was thinking of taking her to another emergency  vet. The only saving grace was the staff in the morning who were much kinder when I ultimately had to put my baby to sleep since she wasn't improving and they couldn't figure what was wrong and she was in a vegetative state. She was pretty much gone and they kept trying to get me to continue paying. It's taken me almost two years to write this review because I wanted to be fair. Again, I am comparing them to other emergency vets I've been to. The lack of communication and how unresponsive they were to how urgent my baby's situation was does make me think her outcome could have been different. I put a lot of blame on myself because I made the choice to take her to this place. All I had to show was thousands of dollars spent which I didn't mind spending. Maybe her outcome would have been the same but it's the way that this was handled. I will never know.

For reference other emergency vet will take your pet back to check vitals, if their stable and determine how urgent their situation is and come out to communicate this to you. They will let you know if they can wait or if it's urgent and what treatment is is needed.

This place had no one at the front desk and it took a bit for someone to finally come out. When they did finally take her to the back no one came out to communicate how her situation was (if she was stable, etc). I had no clue because when I took her things did not look as bad. The person at the front desk just came up to me gave me a generic form(it wasn't  a treatment plan) asking for thousands of dollars to basically get seen first and pay for services she may or may not have needed. They did not tell me this was necessary based on my cat's condition and they didn't communicate her condition either. They even told me it was optional and probably not needed for my cat. When I finally saw the vet it was finally communicated how bad things were.

HORRIFIC - DO NOT TAKE YOUR PET HERE!!!! the worst most unprofessional services I have ever encountered. My dog was vomiting massive amounts of blood at 2am. First they did nothing for 2 hours, then they said they wouldnt give her fluids or anything until I paid $1600, after paying they didnt tell me anything for another 2 hours. They said they saw possibly something on the xrays but wanted to take another 6-8 hours before they would xray her again. Another hour of NO UPDATES they came out to say they wouldnt put her in recovery and give her fluids until I paid another $2700, I ran to get cash and when I came back I asked if they Another hour of NO UPDATES they came out to say they wouldnt put her in recovery and give her fluids until I paid another $2700, I ran to get cash and when I came back I asked if they put her in recovery and they said no not until the payment went through. I went back into room 1 where my stuff was left and they said I couldnt stay I couldnt stay there. I went to the lobby and they said asked why I was still there. I said I wasnt leaving without my dog and they told me I had to wait outside.(NO ONE WAS IN THE BUILDING. IT WAS EMPTY) So I waited outside in my truck for hours and 6 hours later asked for an update and was told" oh no idea we will get to her eventually" another 1 1/2 hours later (NO ONE HAD GIVEN ME ANY UPDATES THIS ENTIRE TIME) they said it looks like she passed it and we can go. I said you charged me for 48 hour of observations. They told me they cant give cash refunds but would send me a check in 3 days.3 days later- nothing
I called and they said oh no its 7 days for a check
7 days later and Adam said oh no it takes weeks for refunds
Today 9/4 - i asked where my refund is and was told they can just give me a check if I drive back down there!!!
I demanded to know why this has never been an option in a month.
I got down there , grabbed my check from the "person in charge samantha sanchez" on my way a guy followed me outside and THREATENED ME TO NEVER GO BACK THERE HE WOULD KILL ME. I drove off and made a report with the LAPD.
the most unprofessional staff! the worst service!!! they didnt even clean my dog up before we left!!!
adam, stephen and samantha were HORRIFIC to deal with!
Every single encounter with their team was very pleasant. Dr. Stikeman was very informative and gave me piece of mind. The facility is beautiful and the services they offer seem amazing.
Took great care if my dog.

Unfortunately, my cat, Artie, needed emergency surgery for an intestinal obstruction, and at the time I brought him to LAASER, they did not have a surgeon available. Despite that, they did everything they could to help us and gave me honest, transparent options, including the possibility of hospitalization.

What truly touched me, though, was that they never tried to keep Artie overnight simply to make more money. Instead, they were completely upfront with me and encouraged me to find another emergency veterinary hospital that could perform the surgery he urgently needed. That level of honesty and compassion meant so much to me during an incredibly frightening and stressful moment.

I especially want to recognize Ellie, their front desk receptionist. She was truly an angel when I needed one. She could see how anxious, overwhelmed, and desperate I was, and instead of simply giving me a list of places to call, she personally stepped in and helped me. She called not one, not two, but multiple emergency veterinary hospitals on my behalf, doing everything she could to make sure Artie received the care he needed.

Ellie will probably never fully understand how much her kindness meant to me that day. When you're scared for your pet and feel completely helpless, having someone show you genuine compassion and go the extra mile can make all the difference in the world.

Thankfully, Artie was able to get his surgery, and he is now doing well. I am incredibly grateful to LAASER for their honesty, compassion, and willingness to put my cat's well-being above everything else.

And Ellie, from the bottom of my heart, thank you. 💙 You were truly a blessing to us during one of the most difficult moments I've experienced as a pet parent. I will never forget your kindness.

This is without a doubt the worst ER vet. I took my dog in because she was acting erratic and experiencing an emergency. I waited for TEN HOURS in my car and in the office from 1am-10am with little to no communication or updates. I was able to talk to a doctor after FIVE HOURS and then waited for another FIVE before hearing anything back. On top of this the doctor who I spoke to was so incredibly, unbelievably rude. I do not understand how anyone could ever hire doctor to be client facing when they are so inconsiderate and lacking empathy. Especially when the client is worried about their pet. They then ordered some tests, wanted my money but didn't explain what any of the tests were or why we needed them. After the TEN HOURS I waited here with no answers, they finally released my dog who seemed to be in the exact same condition as I left her in. But don't worry that was after the doctor snapped at me for not answering my phone and tried to lecture me on phone etiquette. (I was already waiting in the lobby) and let me remind you I had been awake and waiting the entire night until the morning for TEN HOURS. I then gave them $300 for essentially nothing then I took her down the street to VCA in Pasadena where they were able to see her in less than 20 mins. A very knowledgable and considerate doctor sat down with me to very plainly discuss with me all my options and why and they were able to help my dog in less than 40 mins. I felt like I was in WAY better hands at VCA. PLEASE do not go to Laaser, go to VCA if you would really like help.
Extremely nice staff and a very attentive doctor. My little dog suffered sunstroke and received wonderful emergency room treatment that restored him.

I do not recommend this hospital. On Sunday, August 16, 2026, I took my cat to the emergency room because a coyote attacked him in my backyard. This hospital charged us $1,800 just to treat my cat, give him some medicine, and clean the wound. They kept asking for $2,500 for the rest of the night, so we decided to bring my cat home. Thank God he is recovering. When they discharged our cat, they didn't give us any paperwork or anything, and they didn't give us the medicine we paid for. They called me 20 minutes later, but I had already arrived home. Since it was far away, I decided to go back the next day to get my cat's medicine. Very bad service. Never go to this place. So many hours of waiting for such poor service. I do not recommend it at all.

At LAASER Emergency, the facility is clean, the front desk staff is kind and organized, and the vet staff care deeply. Dr. Madden spent a long time with us going over our options and answering all my questions. She approached the conversation with a level head, as well as empathy. It was clear she was passionate about making intentional choices for our babies. She provided us with the resources to give my beloved dog the most humane last day of her life and to ensure she wasn’t in any pain while we spent a little bit of extra time with her. I know vet care is expensive, and I see reviews slamming this facility for that. I did find the fees reasonable and consistent with other LA-based facilities. We live in expensive times, and it’s a shame that care for our little ones isn’t any different. But I didn’t find that LAASER was the outlier by any means.

She never pressured us to make an end of life decision. Not once. But when I questioned whether my decision was the right one, she assured me it was. That assurance stayed with me through the very end. I can’t thank Dr. Madden enough for giving me peace of mind and my baby peace from pain in her last moments. She is truly a top tier doctor and this is a quality facility.

I received a call that my 9 month old golden retriever puppy had collapsed out of nowhere when I was out of town. My friend rushed him to LAASER where he was pronounced dead on arrival.

After a quick scan, the vet told me he died from an enlarged heart.  Right aorta specifically.

One of, if not, the worst moment of my life.

He came with a 2 year health guarantee and the breeder told me to forego the necropsy and that she would be giving me a refund.

Unfortunately she went back on her word and was demanding a necropsy and trying to blame me for the death of my puppy.

The staff here went above and beyond and gave me documentation to support what they found, even tho typically when an animal arrives there after they’re gone, that’s typically all the death certificate will say.

I want to give a special thanks to Lindsay for her care, concern and service during this difficult time.  Steven was also a big help.

Often times Vets, especially emergency vets are all about the money.  I lived near an emergency vet in studio city that had an armed guard 24/7 365 days a year.  Not because the neighborhood was unsafe, but to prevent people from running out on bills.  Do the math and that’s north of $200k a year!

LAASER didn’t issue me a bill.  They held my dogs body for me until I returned the next day and provided me with service above and beyond what can be expected. Thank you so much 💙

I will be making a donation to my favorite shelter in their name!

My senior girl has had so many anal gland problems and she was bleeding a bit. I had to take her and the morning crew, specifically Silene, was so amazing and gentle. They fixed up my dog and she has had a great recovery. Great and reasonable price!
Very bad experience

Im not the type to write reviews but LAASER really took care of my dog and it’s worth sharing. My dog was having an allergic reaction while we were hiking and it was a Sunday so I wasn’t sure where to go. I found LAASER on Google and brought him in. The girls up at the front were nice. I saw a girl walk from the back and she was so gorgeous that I accidentally stopped talking to the girl at the front desk and just stared at her. After I got checked in and they took my dog to the back, I got helped by that same girl, she was the doctor assistant Victoria. I honestly didn’t expect her to have a nice personality because of how pretty she is but she was compassionate and helpful, made me feel less anxious about my dog. She’s not someone you would expect to work in a vet hospital because she should really be a model. You can tell she really cares about what she does. The doctor was Dr Kenny and she was cool too. She answered my questions and was clear about what she was going to do. I expected the bill to be super high but it was a reasonable price. Victoria came to sit next to me while giving me my paperwork and I thought about asking for her number but I didn’t think that was appropriate. I doubt she will remember me but I will never forget her or the way LAASER helped me and my dog

I visited around 9pm 4th of July.  Busy, yet staff was WONDERFUL.  Front desk lady was so personable and efficient, handling a lot of clients with empathy.  Dr. Aghoian-Stubbs is so fantastic - an extremely thorough veterinarian. Addressed my dog's issue quickly, holistically, and also gave great advice for my dog's other routine issues.  The staff understands cost concerns and provides multiple options.  If you need an emergency vet, this is one of the best options in the area.

THANK YOU!!!
At 3:00 am on a Sunday morning in April 2026, my cat, Yoda, had a sudden medical issue. I first called MASH on Santa Monica Blvd; they told me to call LAASER, which I did. They answered right away, and I rushed Yoda over there. It turned out to be a heart and circulatory condition, for which there were no reasonable treatment options.
I made the unexpected and very tough decision to put her down. In a stressful situation, I could not have asked for a better team of people for support. I wish I remember the names of the ER staff and the Veterinarian herself to acknowledge personally. Everyone was attentive, caring and professional. Despite the outcome, I feel grateful LAASER was open and easy to find and work with. I would highly recommend LAASER to anyone.
They even sent me a condolence card which meant so much.

I am sharing this so others are aware of my experience and because I am still waiting for a promised refund one month later.

My baby, Nova, passed away within less than 16 hours of being admitted. She was transferred from urgent care with a recorded temperature of 94°F and placed in a cold oxygen room without blankets. Before any treatment had begun, I was required to pay $6,866.34 upfront.

Throughout her stay, communication was extremely poor. The ER doctor was unable to confirm even basic information about my baby until the time of her passing. I was told I would receive an update after a cardiology consultation, but I was never contacted.

Instead, I was later called to approve an additional heart monitoring procedure costing $582.96. Shortly after that, at 4:52 PM, her heart had already stopped. I was then asked whether I wanted to proceed with CPR, which would have cost an additional $1,200.

I was billed for two days of hospitalization despite the outcome and was informed that a partial refund would be issued. It has now been one month, and I am still waiting with no clear update.

I am deeply disappointed by the lack of communication, transparency, and follow-through during and after this experience.

I am writing this to share my experience with others, and because I have been waiting for the promised partial refund for a month now.

My baby, Nova, passed away less than 16 hours after admission. She was transferred from the emergency room with a temperature of 94°F and placed in a cold oxygen room without a blanket. Before any treatment could begin, I was required to prepay $6,866.34.

Communication was extremely poor throughout the hospitalization. The ER doctor was unable to verify even basic information about my baby until just before her death. Furthermore, although they said they would contact me after a consultation with a cardiologist, I received no contact whatsoever.

Later, I was contacted to approve cardiac monitoring costing an additional $582.96. Shortly thereafter, at 4:52 PM, the baby's heart had already stopped. I was subsequently contacted to choose whether to proceed with CPR, which would incur an additional cost of $1,200.

Consequently, I was charged for two days of hospitalization. Although I was informed that a partial refund would be processed, it has been over a month now, and I am still waiting for the refund without any clear updates.

Overall, this experience left me deeply disappointed regarding the lack of communication, transparency, and inadequate follow-up care.

I brought my puppy, Milo, in because I was concerned he might be experiencing a medical emergency. Upon arrival, we waited approximately 20 minutes before a staff member took him to the back and told us they would evaluate him and prepare a room for us.

After that, we remained in the lobby for about an hour and a half with little to no communication. During that time, I saw numerous other clients come and go, but I received no updates about Milo’s condition or where he was in the process. I eventually had to approach the front desk myself to ask what was happening.

At that point, I was informed that Milo had not yet been seen by a doctor and was simply waiting in a kennel while they waited for another veterinarian to arrive. What was most frustrating was not necessarily the wait itself, but the lack of communication. Had I been informed about the delay from the beginning, I could have made an informed decision about whether to wait, seek care elsewhere, or at least remain with my puppy.

As a pet owner, it was upsetting to learn that Milo had been sitting in a kennel for such a long period without updates while I was under the impression that he was being evaluated. I understand that emergency hospitals must prioritize critical cases and that staffing challenges can occur. However, clients deserve clear communication, realistic expectations, and periodic updates—especially when they are worried about a sick pet.

I hope this feedback helps improve communication and the overall experience for future pet owners.

Up all night with our 9 yr old Cavachon wheezing and coughing. At 5:00 am, I called the hospital and their friendly receptionist said to come down and have him looked at. Their nursing staff were very professional and attentive. Dr Madden was very knowledgeable, treating him with care and proper diagnoses. I was thoroughly impressed with the treatment and communication of updates throughout the morning. I highly recommend Laaser Vet ER for the outstanding service from their nursing staff, doctor’s knowledge and professional experience.

Very disappointing experience. I brought my dog here in early May after she developed IVDD. I specifically requested an MRI, but instead I was told to transfer her to another location and pay for additional services.

The costs were extremely high, and I felt like there was more focus on expensive procedures and additional charges than on addressing my dog's immediate needs. We asked for a pain-relief injection for our dog, but our concerns did not seem to be taken seriously. We felt unheard during a very stressful situation.

I was also uncomfortable seeing that euthanasia procedures appeared to take place behind closed doors without owners being present. That experience was difficult to witness and left a negative impression.

Overall, I expected better communication, compassion, and care. Unfortunately, my experience did not meet those expectations, especially considering the amount we were charged.

We’ve had to take our cat to LAASER three times now and I appreciate them so much. This most recent time we brought him in because he was having a bad reaction to a medication and has advanced kidney disease. One of the vet techs taught us how to give him subcutaneous fluids so we can start doing this process at home to help with his kidney disease, and she was so patient with us while we asked a million questions and navigated this new scary thing. LAASER is a little more expensive than our regular vet and sometimes has longer wait times if there are more urgent cases ahead of us, but that’s to be expected with an emergency vet

was weary of coming here because of the reviews but my frenchie was really scaring me so i brought him in. was only treated with respect from everyone at every point tonight. they comforted me and my baby and were more than clear on my options in terms of payment. thank you so much laaser staff and special thanks to dr lovell

This place is beyond great! Staff is amazing, caring and very compassionate. We got there at 10pm and within 1hr we knew what was going on with our doggie, my daughter was a mess but the staff was very compassionate, attentive and informative.  Great experience for a first timer at a vet hospital.  Thank you !!!

We've been here for emergency services and rehab over the years. Great crew! If you're going here for emergency services it's going to be expensive, but really looking to pet insurance when your critter is young

Cheaper than many other ERs, very friendly staff and reasonable wait times (varies by circumstances obviously). Great rehabilitation team for PT.

Very uncomfortable seating in the lobby

This is the worse place you could take your pet when they need care my puppy could not stand and was vomiting I went to lasser they put me into a room they told me 15m they where gonna be done with test it took them 4h to finish and I payed 300 dollars they didn’t care if my dog was okay if he needed water or nothing then they have the nerve to tell me if I went my dog to stay because his dehydrated maybe bc I got there at 4am and left at 7 30 and they never give my dog water or anything and they wented me to pay 3300 for sum bs took my dog to a different place and he got better
They care more about money then anything like wdym they make me sign sum bs if my dog about to die they gonna try to bring him back and make me pay 1600

It’s been years since I came here but I still get so angry when I drive by it. They saved my dog but they bled me dry. Do not come here unless you are made of money.
To the reply:  while I consented to everything, it doesn’t mean you guys aren’t overpriced and take advantage of people trying to save their pets
Arrived at 10am 4hrs later...still in the waiting room when I arrived 1 person ahead of me...no one communicates

Pretty responsive given the situation and were willing to accommodate a procedure that was not in their billing system.  Many other vets simply could not do this very basic procedure for whatever reason.

My cat needed to have a two day stay and two blood transfusions. Despite having a busier week than normal from another ER closing, they were able to provide timely updates from both techs and the vet every time I called.

Three vets worked with my cat over the two days (24 hour service), and each was pleasant to speak with. They answered any questions I had over the phone, and called back relatively quickly when the vet was unavailable.

At the point of discharge, they let me know that they were providing a refund as they used less liquid and medication than predicted. Another ER could have easily taken advantage and kept the money.

Our dog just ate some raisins, a friend suggested we bring the dog here, and they were so nice.  There was no wait when we went in, and the charge was very modest, lower than any other emergency vet we've been to.
The kindest people in the most difficult time. Thank God for them.

The only reason I am giving 2 stars instead of 1 is because LAASER did ok treating my dog initially.

Internal medicine is only there 9-4 M-W.

In February we took our sweet Arya to LAASER after her liver levels skyrocketed & she stopped eating. We brought her in on a Monday so Internal Medicine was able to do an ultrasound on her Tuesday morning. They found she had an inflamed liver. She had the symptoms of excessive thirst & urinary incontinence. I asked if diabetes / cushings disease should be considered & I was told no. We were able to bring her home after an overnight stay & were told they didn't know what was wrong with her, but maybe it was an infection that spread to her liver. They sent her home with a course of antibiotics & asked us to come back 2 weeks later.

2 weeks later her liver levels were still very elevated. We brought back up that her urinary incontinence was a new development &that she still was peeing & drinking a lot. Asked again about cushings & diabetes & they said they didn't think that was it, but it was a possibility. They ran a test costing several hundred dollars (at this point we had already spent thousands) to test if her urethra was too relaxed?? & gave us a bill of another 1K. Asked us to come back in another 2weeks to test her liver levels again.

We wanted my card on file since the insurance we have is in my name. They proceeded to text, email & call us repeatedly that next 24 hours saying they wouldn't send the test if I did not pay. I paid.

Everything happened so fast.
On July 30th, my cat Mop started vomiting white foam frequently and barely responded when I called him. At 4 a.m., I rushed him to the emergency room. He was diagnosed with pancreatitis, and within less than a day, his liver began to fail.

I told the doctors, “Save his life, no matter the cost.” I was ready with all the money in the world—whatever it took to bring him back, I was willing.
But just three days later, on August 1st, Mop passed away.

Since then, I’ve been replaying everything in my head. I’ve spoken to multiple vets, shared his medical records, and I still can’t forgive myself. Why didn’t I notice it earlier? If I had kept him at home instead of rushing him to the hospital, would he have lived longer? Was this a medical error?

He had annual check-ups, was fully vaccinated, and ate the best quality high-protein food. So why did this happen?

I made countless phone calls, trying to find answers.
The hospital’s conclusion was hepatic encephalopathy caused by pancreatitis-induced liver damage.
But just on the 29th, he was still lying on my lap purring and cuddling. Even on the 31st, when he was already declared critical, he still meowed at me.

At 11:35 p.m. on August 1st, they told me his blood pressure had crashed. CPR failed. He passed away.
When I saw him for the last time, his body was still warm—but the breath was gone.

I’ve learned that money can’t fix everything.

Now his sister, Riceball, has noticed her brother is gone. She’s eating less, sitting quietly in the spots he used to nap. Her tiny head doesn’t understand death—only that her brother hasn’t come back in a very long time.
The only thing keeping me going right now is that she still needs me. She lost her brother, and I have to stay strong to take care of her.

So to every cat parent out there, please:
Pay attention to even the smallest changes.
Even if it’s just a slight loss of appetite, a little vomiting, or slower reactions—don’t brush it off. Cats are masters of hiding pain. By the time we notice something’s wrong, it might already be too late.

Do the check-ups. Don’t delay blood work or ultrasounds.
It’s not “they’re too young to worry” or “they look fine”—early detection can literally save their life.

I hope none of you ever have to go through what I did.
But if someday the worst does happen, I hope you’ll catch it earlier, and act faster than I could.

They can’t speak, but they’re always trying to tell us something.
